Key is sent in the body rather than a header.

terms.meaning: to fill in a record with more details from an outside source

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Service header
sections.what: Names the contact-finder service and links to its documentation.
sections.why: Records where the rules come from.

sections.name: ApolloPerson
sections.title: Person record shape
sections.what: Describes one person Apollo returns: name, title, email, LinkedIn link, location and company.
sections.why: Gives the app one predictable shape for contacts.
sections.watch_out: Every field is optional, so callers must handle missing values.

sections.name: ApolloSearchResult
sections.title: Search result shape
sections.what: The result of a people search: a list of people and a total count.
sections.why: Lets the app show results and how many exist.
sections.watch_out: A total of zero may mean the count was missing, so do not treat zero as proof of no matches.

sections.name: apolloPeopleSearch
sections.title: Searching for people at a company
sections.what: Searches Apollo for people at a company, filtered by titles and locations, and returns one page of matches.
sections.why: Finds people to contact at target companies.
sections.watch_out: The API key is in the request body and each search may use paid credits.

sections.name: apolloEnrichPerson
sections.title: Looking up one person
sections.what: Finds one person by email, LinkedIn link, or name and company, and returns the full profile, or nothing if there is no match.
sections.why: Turns a partial contact into a fuller record. The code deliberately turns off personal email reveal, and the reason is not stated.
sections.watch_out: A null result is normal, so callers must check for it before using the record.

summary: Client for the Apollo contact service, used to find people at companies and to look up one person's full profile.
purpose: Helps the user find decision makers to contact at target companies.
why: Reason for the design is not stated in the code. The file header only names the service.
how: 1. Searches for people by company name or domain, optionally filtered by job titles and locations. 2. Looks up one person by email, LinkedIn link or name and company. 3. Returns null if no match exists for a lookup. 4. Throws errors that include the service's status and message for other failures.
inputs: An Apollo API key, plus search filters such as company name, domain, titles and locations, or lookup details such as email or LinkedIn link.
outputs: A search result with a list of people and a total count, or a single person record, or null when no person is found.
risks: The API key is sent inside the request body, so it could appear in logs. Each search and lookup may use paid credits in the service. Personal emails are not requested.
debug: A missing key error points to the settings page. A status code in the error message shows what the service rejected. If searches return nothing, check the company name or domain and title filters.
